K1.stone_why: Faceted bold caps, Squat and set numbers read as hewn inscription, though the regular titles stay a smooth bookish serif.
K1.carving_why: Facets on S, O, 0 and 3/8 are crisp, but the 6 in 62.5 is mostly round with only a few facets so it looks pasted on next to the polygonal 5 and O, and the O/0 are slightly lumpy.
K1.calm_why: Moderate weight and generous serifs keep it steady; the angular bold is present without shouting.
K1.personality_why: The chiselled polygonal bounds give a recognisable voice, slightly diluted by the inconsistent 6.

K2.stone_why: A clean classical serif with Roman-inscription proportions but no cut or hewn quality at any size.
K2.carving_why: No visible carving; all curves are smooth outlines.
K2.calm_why: Very calm, even and legible with solid presence in the bold numbers.
K2.personality_why: Pleasant but generic book serif one would not recognise again.

K3.stone_why: Same faceted bold display as K1, reading as chiselled stone in Squat, SISIFO and the set numbers, with smooth regular titles.
K3.carving_why: The 6 is faceted like the 5, S, 3, 8 and O, so the bold digits share one coherent cut; facets are crisp though O/0 remain a touch uneven and 0/O stay distinguishable by width.
K3.calm_why: Steady weight and open spacing; angularity adds presence without aggression.
K3.personality_why: Distinct chiselled-polygon voice applied more consistently than K1.

K4.stone_why: Heavier weight with faceting through the regular titles too gives the strongest monumental, carved-block feel.
K4.carving_why: Coherent facets across S, 3, 5, 6, 8 and caps, crisp and deliberate, though the heavy 0 and O are somewhat blobby-polygonal and the cuts get coarser at bold weight.
K4.calm_why: Strong presence but the dark display and heavy 13 px body tip toward loud and dense.
K4.personality_why: Most distinctive and memorable: a dense hewn-stone face carried through every size.
